subject: DPA: EU-US transfer method + backup/DR carveout — redlines and e-sign path
body:
Message 1/6
From: Tom Bailey <t.bailey@quantfinance.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@quantfinance.com>
Date: 2026-11-20 09:12 PST
Subject: Redwood DPA + backup carveout questions

Jonas —

Thanks for sending over the DPA draft during the procurement call. Our legal team is reviewing but flagged a couple of items we need clarified before we can route for signature:

- Data transfer mechanism: we prefer EU Standard Contractual Clauses plus a supplementary technical measures note. Can your team confirm that SCCs are an acceptable transfer mechanism (we saw international transfer language but not the exact method)?
- Backup / DR carveout: we understand retention for backups for DR purposes is common, but we need a clear maximum timeframe and commitments on scope, encryption, and access logging. Our security policy requires a 60-day maximum retention for backups containing customer data (unless otherwise approved).
- Subprocessors list and notification SLA — please provide the current list and confirm a 30-day notice before new subprocessor goes live.

We'd like to get the DPA executed by the end of next week if possible. Could you route to your privacy/compliance folks and confirm the e-sign path (DocuSign or AdobeSign)?

Best,
Tom
Head of Procurement — QuantFinance

---
Message 2/6
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20 10:05 PST
Subject: Fwd: Redwood DPA + backup carveout questions

Forwarding Tom's note — can you weigh in on our standard positions and whether we're willing to accept a 60-day backup retention for DR? Also confirm SCCs vs. other transfer approaches.

My inclination: accept SCCs + documented technical controls, allow a limited backup retention carveout (we usually say 90 days for full image backups, 30 days for logical backups). If we can agree to 60 days for backups tied to DR with encryption and strict access controls, that would probably close quickly.

Jonas
Sr. Director, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

---
Message 3/6
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-20 11:28 PST
Subject: RE: Fwd: Redwood DPA + backup carveout questions

Team —

Thanks for the context. Quick positions and proposed language that I drafted (attached as Redlined DPA v3):

1) Transfer mechanism: we can accept EU SCCs (2021 module) as the primary transfer mechanism for QuantFinance with an explicit note that our technical and organizational measures (listed in SCC Annex II) supplement the SCCs. We'll attach "SCC_addendum.pdf" (see attachment) and reference that the parties will rely on SCCs and equivalent safeguards for transfers.

2) Backup/DR carveout: we will agree to a limited carveout with the following constraints:
   - Maximum retention in backups: 60 days for backups that include Customer Data (applies to logical and encrypted snapshots used for DR and restore).
   - Backups will be encrypted at rest with customer-specific keys when requested (KMS integration), and access will be limited to named personnel (security ops + on-call) and logged.
   - Restores that result in data being processed outside agreed regions must be approved by Customer.
   - Redwood will attempt deletion of backup copies on a rolling basis after 60 days and will notify Customer of any exceptional holds (legal/regulatory holds) within 5 business days.

3) Subprocessors notice: we currently provide 30 days' notice for new subprocessors. We will attach the current list (subprocessors_list_20261120.csv) and commit to notify QuantFinance 30 days prior to onboard.

4) Execution: We prefer DocuSign for speed but accept AdobeSign if required. We'll provide a DocuSign packet once redlines are agreed.

Please review attached redline (Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.pdf) — I've highlighted the backup carveout language and SCC addendum.

- Laura Bennett
  Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
  Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: Redlined DPA v3 (Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.pdf), Subprocessors list (subprocessors_list_20261120.csv), SCC_addendum.pdf

Message 4/6
From: Lucia Marin <lucia.marin@stabilitysys.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Bailey <t.bailey@quantfinance.com>, Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@quantfinance.com>
Date: 2026-11-23 15:02 PST
Subject: RE: DPA: EU-US transfer method + backup/DR carveout — redlines and e-sign path

Hi all —

Thanks for the redline and the proposed positions. A few notes from QuantFinance Legal:

- SCCs are fine provided Redwood accepts an additional warranty that the SCCs are the primary legal basis and that Redwood will implement the technical measures as attached. We need the SCC annex to be physically attached to the DPA.
- Backup retention: 60 days is acceptable in principle, but we need: (a) a defined scope of "backup" (system image vs. logical DB dump) and (b) a firm deletion/refresh guarantee — specifically, that backups will be expunged no later than 60 days and that the deletion process is auditable.
- Access logging: we require immutable logs for any restores and admin access for 12 months.
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is acceptable; however, we request an opt-out right for specific categories (e.g., if a subprocessor is in a sanctioned country).

If you can incorporate the SCC annex and tighten the backup deletion verification steps (we can accept the 5 business-day notification for holds but need the deletion as auditable), we can circulate internally and aim to sign by next Friday.

Regards,
Lucia Marin
Senior Counsel, QuantFinance

---
Message 5/6
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-24 09:46 PST
Subject: RE: DPA: EU-US transfer method + backup/DR carveout — redlines and e-sign path

Lucia / Tom —

We're aligned on the main asks. To be explicitly clear, proposed final language we can commit to is below (I'll paste for clarity as we finalize the DocuSign packet):

- Backup scope: "Backup" means copies of Customer Data taken for disaster recovery purposes including encrypted snapshots (block-level) and logical backups (database exports) that are maintained solely for restore operations.
- Retention: "Redwood will retain backups containing Customer Data for no longer than sixty (60) days from the date of creation, unless a legally-binding hold is applied. Redwood will delete backups on a rolling basis in accordance with its documented deletion process and will provide Customer with confirmation of deletion upon request. Deletion operations will be logged and verifiable."
- Encryption & keys: "Backups will be encrypted at rest. Customer may request KMS-backed encryption; requests will be subject to Redwood's documented integration timeline (typical lead time 10 business days)."
- Access & logs: "Access to backups or restore operations is limited to named security and SRE personnel; all access and restore actions will be recorded in tamper-evident logs and retained for twelve (12) months."
- Subprocessors: "Redwood will provide 30 days' advance notice of new subprocessors and will not add subprocessors in restricted jurisdictions subject to export or sanctions laws without Customer consent. Customer may object to a new subprocessor within 10 business days; if unresolved, parties will escalate to senior counsel for resolution."

If QuantFinance confirms these bullet points, Laura can incorporate the language into the DPA and I'll prepare the SCC annex and the technical controls doc to attach. We will then send a DocuSign packet.

Neha Kapoor
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

---
Message 6/6
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Tom Bailey <t.bailey@quantfinance.com>, Lucia Marin <lucia.marin@stabilitysys.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-27 17:45 PST
Subject: Final DPA language agreed — DocuSign packet live

Tom / Lucia —

Thanks for the quick turn. Per Neha and Laura's language, QuantFinance's updates are reflected and we have attached the SCC annex and the technical measures doc. We're comfortable with:

- SCCs (2021) as the transfer mechanism + SCC annex attached
- 60-day maximum backup retention for DR (scope defined; deletion logged and verifiable)
- Encryption at rest and KMS option per request (lead time noted)
- 12-month immutable access logs for restore/admin events
- 30-day notice for subprocessors and opt-out/escalation path for restricted jurisdictions

DocuSign packet is ready: https://app.docusign.com/packages/ABC-123-QuantFinance (attached as DocuSign_Packet_RWI-4879.pdf stub). Please review and sign — we've set signers as QuantFinance Legal (Lucia) and QuantFinance Procurement (Tom).

Next steps:
- QuantFinance to sign in DocuSign
- Redwood to countersign immediately upon QuantFinance signing
- Post-signature: Redwood will provide the SCC annex and a confirmation email with the subprocessors snapshot as of signing date

If you prefer AdobeSign, reply-all and we'll switch the packet. Otherwise we'll proceed with DocuSign.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Sr. Director, Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs included in thread: Redwood_DPA_v3_redline.pdf; subprocessors_list_20261120.csv; SCC_addendum.pdf; DocuSign_Packet_RWI-4879.pdf
